thinkingSteps.title: Brute force idea
thinkingSteps.body: For “Design Twitter”, first say a correct slow approach: scan or retry every candidate until the example works by hand. Input post/follow/unfollow/getNewsFeed sequence should still produce recent followed tweets.

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: See code.

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: To design a simplified version of Twitter, we can use a combination of data structures. We maintain a dictionary to map users to their tweets, and a set of followees for each user. When a user posts a tweet, we add it to their tweet list. When a user wants to retrieve their news feed, we merge their own tweets and the tweets of their followees, and then sort them based on timestamps.

thinkingSteps.title: Better idea
thinkingSteps.body: Commit to Heap / priority queue. Repeatedly need min or max quickly. Walk example `post/follow/unfollow/getNewsFeed sequence` → `recent followed tweets` while naming each variable, then code. Close with See code time and See code space.
